summary:
Mission Nova is an interactive educational web application designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of living and working on the Moon.

Players take on the role of a junior astronaut responsible for managing a lunar habitat. Through a series of mission decisions, they explore essential space systems, including life support, radiation protection, energy management, and food production.

The simulation demonstrates how limited resources and engineering trade-offs influence mission safety and sustainability. Each decision provides educational feedback to help players understand the scientific principles behind their choices.

By combining interactive gameplay, space science, and creative web design, Mission Nova aims to make STEM education more engaging, accessible, and inspiring for the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Mission Nova – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. Project Overview

Mission Nova is an interactive, browser-based educational simulation designed to introduce young learners to the scientific and engineering challenges of living and working on the Moon.

Players take on the role of a junior astronaut mission commander responsible for managing a lunar habitat and protecting their crew during a seven-day mission. Through interactive decision-making, the simulation encourages students to explore essential space systems, understand resource limitations, and develop practical problem-solving skills.

2. How It Works

Mission Nova features five interconnected resource management systems:

  • Oxygen: Maintains the crew's breathable air supply.
  • Power: Supports essential equipment and habitat operations.
  • Water: Provides resources for life support and daily activities.
  • Food: Represents the crew's nutritional supply.
  • Radiation Shielding: Protects astronauts from hazardous space radiation.

Each mission day, players select one engineering action, such as generating oxygen, charging batteries, growing food, reinforcing the habitat, or recycling water.

Every decision involves benefits and resource costs. For example, generating oxygen increases the oxygen supply but consumes electrical power and water.

Players must also respond to simulated emergencies, including solar storms and life-support leaks. These events require additional decisions that influence the safety and sustainability of the mission.

The simulation includes interactive resource indicators, mission progress tracking, educational explanations, and a final performance score.

The primary objective is to keep all five critical systems operational throughout the seven-day mission.

3. Innovation and Creativity

Mission Nova combines interactive gameplay, space science education, and resource management into an engaging learning experience.

Rather than simply presenting scientific information, the application allows students to explore the consequences of engineering decisions.

Its main creative features include:

  • Interactive lunar habitat resource management.
  • Engineering decisions with interconnected consequences.
  • Simulated emergency scenarios requiring critical thinking.
  • Real-time visual feedback and mission progress indicators.
  • Educational explanations connecting gameplay with space science.
  • Mission completion results that encourage reflection and improvement.

This approach helps transform complex space exploration concepts into accessible learning activities.

4. Technology and Development Tools

Mission Nova was developed using Visual Studio Code (VS Code), HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.

HTML5: Provides the structure for the mission dashboard, resource indicators, engineering actions, emergency scenarios, and educational content.

CSS3: Controls the application's visual appearance, responsive layout, colour scheme, interactive elements, and resource progress bars.

JavaScript: Implements the gameplay logic, resource calculations, engineering decisions, emergency events, mission progression, and final performance scoring.

Visual Studio Code: Used as the primary development environment for writing, editing, organizing, and testing the source code.

GitHub: Used to store and manage the project's source files.

GitHub Pages: Used to deploy and host the publicly accessible web application.

The application runs directly in a modern web browser without requiring installation, registration, or specialized hardware.

Live Application: https://jannatulrupa1999.github.io/mission-nova/

5. Educational Impact

Mission Nova aims to inspire young learners to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

The project supports learning through interactive experimentation and decision-making.

Its intended educational benefits include:

  • Developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Understanding resource conservation and sustainability.
  • Exploring basic life-support and energy management concepts.
  • Recognizing the importance of engineering trade-offs.
  • Encouraging curiosity about lunar exploration and future space missions.

By making space science more interactive and accessible, Mission Nova seeks to encourage the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.

6. Scientific Foundation and Limitations

Mission Nova draws educational inspiration from publicly available NASA resources, including NASA Humans in Space, the Artemis programmed, and NASA Learning Resources.

These resources provide background information about human space exploration, lunar missions, and the challenges associated with sustaining astronauts beyond Earth.

The simulation is an educational model rather than a NASA-approved mission planning or engineering tool.

Resource percentages, action costs, emergency events, and performance scores are fictional game-design parameters created to demonstrate simplified engineering relationships. They do not represent measured NASA mission values or validated engineering calculations.

The application provides links to NASA resources for further scientific learning.

7. Development and Attribution

Mission Nova was developed by team NASA_Ade_1 for the 2026 NASA International Space Apps Challenge, under the challenge Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The project combines web development, interactive simulation, educational storytelling, and space science concepts.

AI assistance was used for research support, programming guidance, code development assistance, content drafting, and documentation. The project was developed and tested by the team.

All external resources and development tools are acknowledged in the project submission.

Mission Nova is an independent educational project and is not an official NASA product.
